Shabelle irrigation and access to Mogadishu markets provide food and income options, but displacement settlements and insecure rural supply routes raise gamma and limit the upward adjustment to p. Flood cycles, farm-labour seasonality and population movements support an elevated omega.

Cattle pastoralism, inland livestock production and some riverine farming expose poorer households to asset and purchasing-power constraints, supporting elevated gamma. Rural treatment distances motivate a modest p, while seasonal pasture, livestock prices and insecure trading routes support elevated omega.

Juba pump irrigation and livestock production offer complementary livelihoods, but insecure access and dependence on irrigation inputs motivate elevated gamma and a restrained p. River-level changes, floods, crop calendars and transport disruptions support a high omega.

Cattle pastoralism, rainfed farming and coastal activities diversify production, but remoteness and persistent insecurity motivate elevated gamma and a lower p. Seasonal livestock and crop income, rainfall variability and disrupted trade support elevated omega.

West Golis pastoralism and northwestern agropastoral production offer several food pathways, supporting a relatively lower gamma. Rural distances restrain p, while seasonal grazing, crop production and purchased-grain prices imply moderate omega.

Shabelle irrigation, cowpea farming and proximity to Mogadishu create income options, but insecure road access and exposed agricultural households motivate elevated gamma and a moderate p. River flooding, harvest cycles and recurrent supply-route disruptions support elevated omega.

Mogadishu's markets and concentration of health providers support a relatively higher p, while established displacement settlements and insecure livelihoods keep gamma elevated. Repeated arrivals, evictions, food-price movements and interruptions to household income support elevated omega despite urban diversification.

_metadata.status: Subjective structural elicitation scenario; not empirically calibrated district rate estimates.

interpretation.p: Monthly probability of leaving the modeled state for any reason; service access is used only as a proxy for recovery opportunity. It is not a treatment success probability.
interpretation.gamma: Monthly new arrivals divided by the under-5 population, expressed as a fraction.
interpretation.omega: Total standard deviation of monthly new arrivals divided by the under-5 population, expressed as a fraction; no additional baseline variance is to be added to this parameter.
interpretation.time_invariance: Each district has one constant parameter triple representing background conditions across 2017–2021; seasonal and shock-driven departures belong to the likelihood.
interpretation.scope: Each entry represents the historical district as a whole, including urban and rural populations; mixed livelihood descriptions are qualitative and are not population-weighted zone estimates.

elicitation.numeric_basis: The contextual sources motivate relative differences. They do not identify absolute monthly incidence, duration or arrival standard deviations. All numerical centres and concentrations below are explicit analyst-selected assumptions, not quantities estimated from those documents.
elicitation.p_centres: Centres range from 0.18 for severely constrained settings to 0.34 for major accessible urban service environments, corresponding approximately to 5.6 to 2.9 months under the stipulated 1/p convention. No mortality-related upward adjustment or spontaneous-recovery adjustment was imposed without independent evidence.
elicitation.gamma_centres: Centres range from 0.0040 to 0.0105 per month. Higher assumptions reflect persistent displacement exposure, insecure livelihoods, restricted access or flood-exposed food systems; diversification motivates lower assumptions. These anchors were not obtained by multiplying an observed stock by an exit rate.
elicitation.omega_centres: Centres range from 0.0015 to 0.0048, selected for recurring seasonal, climatic, movement and market mechanisms. Thin evidence changes concentration only and does not increase the centre.
elicitation.beta_conversion: For centre m and concentration k, a=m*k and b=(1-m)*k; mean=a/(a+b), variance=m*(1-m)/(k+1).
elicitation.informativeness: Concentrations intentionally impose informative marginals as requested. Their strength is a modeling choice, not a claim that the structural evidence warrants this degree of numerical confidence. Large a+b for small-scale fractions is not equivalent to equally many observed children.
elicitation.independence: Only marginal priors are elicited. A product of the three Betas additionally assumes prior independence, which is not established by the sources.
elicitation.model_fit_limit: A single omega averages recurring process variability across the period. The supplied six-month variance formula additionally requires assumptions about cross-month arrival covariance; recurring seasonality can create dependence not represented by independent monthly shocks.

outcome_separation.used_for_calibration: Structural context only; no observed or reported acute-malnutrition outcomes were used to choose centres or concentrations.
outcome_separation.retrieval_incident: Some broad search responses incidentally exposed prohibited outcome snippets. Those snippets and their outcome descriptions were discarded; the associated material was not used as evidence. This is not a claim of an exposure-free retrieval process.
outcome_separation.restricted_reports: Nutrition survey reports and their tables, maps, classifications and burden estimates were not intentionally opened or used.
outcome_separation.programme_endogeneity: No programme allocation, facility count selected by nutritional need, or treatment-admission total was used as a proxy for incidence. Generic health-system access and humanitarian movement constraints were used qualitatively.

evidence_limits.chronic_afi_baseline: A comparable district-by-district typical IPC Acute Food Insecurity phase for all seasons in 2017–2021 was not verified. No district was assigned a chronic phase from a single seasonal classification, and no numeric phase uplift was applied.
evidence_limits.cmam_and_health: District CMAM coverage, supply continuity, skilled attendance, health-facility density and chronic under-5 mortality were not verified comprehensively. p differences are qualitative urban/rural/access inferences, not measured coverage effects.
evidence_limits.exit_mechanisms: The available context does not identify the relative roles of recovery and death in district exit probabilities. A district-specific acute-and-fatal versus chronic-and-persistent phenotype is therefore unverified; lower p in restricted settings encodes an assumed persistence mechanism, not a measured natural history.
evidence_limits.displacement: Primary contextual evidence verifies several receiving centres, but complete historical district IDP population shares were not retrieved. No large-hosting claim or incidence uplift was applied to every district merely because it contains a town.
evidence_limits.livelihood_age: The 2016 profiles consolidate baselines from different, sometimes much earlier reference years. They establish broad structural patterns but do not verify that every detail remained constant through 2021.
evidence_limits.district_detail: Several smaller or remote districts rely on broad zone and regional context rather than direct district programme evidence. Their prior concentrations are reduced, and district-specific claims should be treated as inferences.
evidence_limits.validation_needed: Absolute rate calibration and the imposed informativeness remain unvalidated. Sensitivity to lower concentration and alternative absolute anchors is required before treating these priors as operationally established.

source_access_audit.alternative: Read the 2016 consolidated livelihood profiles, the 2015 joint livelihood map and separable Guban/East Golis descriptions. Standalone West Golis and several older profile downloads failed; S01 supplied their structural alternatives.

source_access_audit.requested: FEWS NET Somalia country page and livelihood pages
source_access_audit.status: Country page and direct livelihood landing page returned HTTP 403.
source_access_audit.alternative: Read the joint FSNAU–FEWS NET profile and map on FSNAU, plus separable contextual excerpts from the FEWS NET-hosted May 2021 brief.

source_access_audit.requested: FSNAU publications and multiyear seasonal sequence
source_access_audit.status: Publications index accessible; a complete 2017–2021 sequence of safe contextual sections was not reviewed. Several climate bulletin downloads were inaccessible.
source_access_audit.alternative: Used pre-period livelihood seasonality and separable 2021 climate, conflict and market mechanisms, corroborated by 2018 and 2020 access evidence. Did not assert a calculated multiyear food-insecurity baseline.

source_access_audit.status: SARA catalogue accessible, full PDF downloads unavailable or verification-blocked; comprehensive district CMAM assessment unavailable.
source_access_audit.alternative: Read WHO's health-system section and its discussion of the 2016 assessment, using rural access and urban provider concentration only as qualitative proxies.
Read primary OCHA documents through mirrors: 2020 access overview and the separable December 2018 access section.

source_access_audit.status: The attempted UNHCR May 2021 displacement PDF and 2020 CCCM annual PDF were inaccessible. Some IOM pages and Doolow's direct report also failed.
source_access_audit.alternative: Read UN-hosted IOM displacement context, UN Somalia's 2020 hosting context and IOM's 2019 Kismaayo movement summary; use the indexed IOM Doolow summary only as limited corroboration. No post-2021 displacement totals were projected backward.

sources.used: General rural and nomadic access barriers, urban provider concentration, workforce shortages and medicine supply constraints; these are contextual proxies, not measured district CMAM coverage.

sources.used: Regional restrictions on movement and services, insecure transport, town encirclement and interruption of air access; regional evidence does not establish identical conditions throughout each district.

sources.title: OCHA, Somalia Humanitarian Bulletin, December 2018, access section
sources.used: Recurring blockades affecting named towns, Belet Xaawo road restrictions and the longstanding Bulo Burto blockade; source administrative-label errors were not adopted.

sources.used: Persistent displacement hosting, insecure housing, constrained livelihoods and limited services in peripheral settlements in Baydhaba, Bossaso and Mogadishu.

sources.used: Baydhaba's protracted hosting role, movement from rural Bay, repeated evictions and site hygiene risks.

sources.used: Seasonal river and rainfall mechanisms, named transport disruptions, resource conflicts and agricultural labour seasonality; one seasonal food-insecurity classification was not treated as a chronic baseline.

sources.used: Corroboration only: recurrent flooding and weak embankments; primary livelihood profiles and S08 supply the main riverine evidence.

sources.used: Displacement-receiving role of Kismaayo and variable movements from Jamaame associated with insecurity and food access.
